problem: The formula V_terminal = EMF − I(R_internal + polarization) adds a voltage (polarization) to a resistance, which is dimensionally wrong. Internal resistance drops IR volts, while polarization is itself a voltage drop.
fix: V_terminal = EMF − I·R_internal − V_polarization, where R_internal is in ohms, I is the current in amperes and V_polarization is the polarization (overvoltage) in volts. If you prefer a resistance form, write it as R_polarization and say it is an equivalent resistance.

problem: LiFePO₄ is listed as an alternative cathode but the cell voltage is then given as 3.6–3.8 V for any Li-ion cell. LiFePO₄ cells give about 3.2–3.3 V, so a student may apply 3.7 V to an LFP cell.
fix: One cell gives about 3.6–3.8 V with a layered oxide cathode such as LiCoO₂; an LiFePO₄ cell gives about 3.2–3.3 V.

problem: "The lead sulfate is the active change" is vague; students may not see that it means both plates are converted to PbSO₄.
fix: The key change on discharge is that both plates are converted to lead sulfate (PbSO₄) and the acid is diluted.
